title: fix: reject isolated completion observed after capture deadline
body:
When `communicate()` finishes normally after the isolated module budget has expired, the runner previously accepted its valid completion receipt and returned success. Check the deadline at that return boundary and reuse the existing timeout/ownership cleanup. A late capture now returns 124 with its exact stdout/stderr and the existing timeout diagnostic. The separate bounded drain after an on-time observed leader exit remains permitted.

The regression uses a real unittest subprocess, genuine completion receipt and binary stdout/stderr. Only the parent runner clock advances at the successful capture boundary; it models a parent scheduling pause and does not infer the child's physical exit timestamp. Before/equal/after-budget and unlimited controls distinguish the policy. Removing the three-line guard restores exactly the equal/after false successes. A real inherited-pipe fixture verifies post-stop drain grace.

Validation on macOS 27 arm64 / Python 3.14.6: seven focused modules under normal Python and `-O`, 64.126 seconds total, all runnable tests pass. Per mode: 55 discovered, 32 executed and 23 platform skips. The macOS kqueue tests observe actual owned-child exit. Commands:

```sh
for module in test_isolated_test_deadlines test_research_isolated_test_posix_pipes test_isolated_test_capture_finalization test_isolated_test_cancellation test_research_worker_failure_order test_isolated_test_exit_cleanup test_isolated_test_windows_exit; do
  python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p "$module.py" -v
  python3 -B -O -m unittest discover -s tests -p "$module.py" -v
done
git diff --check
```

Base: `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`. [Advance claim #6094](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6094). Credit Tekalign's optional module deadlines, Nick Petalas's ownership fixtures, and the retained POSIX pipe-observation and capture-finalization work. JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. This is a shared tooling repair; no frozen source, scientific claim, selected result or test-discovery coverage changes.

Open next questions: run the same focused checks on native Windows and Linux; those platform-specific results are not established here. Full historical/scientific replay and package export were unnecessary for this two-file runner repair and were not run. Hosted CI/publication remain pending root review.
